questions.q: What is the electron configuration of Fe (Z = 26)?
questions.why: 26 electrons: [Ar] 4s² 3d⁶.

questions.q: Why is the first ionisation energy of oxygen lower than that of nitrogen?
o: The paired electrons in oxygen's 2p orbital repel each other
Oxygen's electron is in a higher shell
questions.why: Spin-pair repulsion in one 2p orbital makes that electron easier to remove.

questions.q: Which particle has 10 electrons and 11 protons?
questions.why: Sodium (Z = 11) that has lost one electron.

questions.q: How many molecules are in 0.25 mol of CO₂? (L = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
A compound is 40.0% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass. What is its empirical formula?
What is the percentage yield if 8.0 g is made and 10.0 g was expected?
What is the shape of an ammonia molecule?
questions.why: Three bonding pairs and one lone pair: pyramidal, bond angle about 107°.

questions.q: What is the bond angle in methane?
questions.why: Four bonding pairs repel equally: tetrahedral, 109.5°.

questions.q: Why does water have an unusually high boiling point for its size?
questions.why: O–H…O hydrogen bonds are much stronger than other intermolecular forces.

questions.q: Which molecule is non-polar overall even though it has polar bonds?
questions.why: CO₂ is linear; the two bond dipoles cancel.

questions.q: Real gases behave most like ideal gases at…
questions.why: Molecules are far apart and fast, so their volume and attractions matter less.

questions.q: Using pV = nRT, what are the units of V?
questions.why: With p in Pa and R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, V must be in m³.

questions.q: Hess's law is based on conservation of…
questions.why: The enthalpy change is independent of the route taken.

questions.q: 50.0 g of water rises by 6.0 °C. How much energy was transferred? (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹)
Standard enthalpy change of combustion is always…
questions.why: Combustion releases energy, so it is exothermic.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of Mn in KMnO₄?
questions.why: K +1, four O −2 each: Mn = +7.

questions.q: In Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + Br₂, what is oxidised?
questions.why: Br⁻ loses electrons (oxidation number −1 → 0).

questions.q: Adding a catalyst to an equilibrium…
o: makes equilibrium reached faster but doesn't move it
questions.why: A catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally.

questions.q: For an exothermic forward reaction, raising the temperature makes Kc…
questions.why: The equilibrium shifts to the endothermic (reverse) direction, so Kc falls.

questions.q: A Brønsted–Lowry acid is a…
questions.why: Acids donate H⁺; bases accept them.

questions.q: On a Boltzmann distribution, raising the temperature…
o: moves the peak left and up
moves the peak right and down, with more molecules above Ea
reduces the area under the curve
questions.why: More molecules have energy at or above the activation energy; the total area stays the same.

questions.q: A catalyst works by…
o: providing an alternative route with a lower activation energy
questions.why: More particles then have enough energy to react.

questions.q: Across Period 3, atomic radius…
questions.why: Nuclear charge rises with similar shielding, pulling the electrons closer.

questions.q: Which Period 3 oxide is amphoteric?
questions.why: Al₂O₃ reacts with both acids and bases.

questions.q: Down Group 2, the solubility of the hydroxides…
questions.why: Mg(OH)₂ is sparingly soluble; Ba(OH)₂ is much more soluble.

questions.q: Down Group 2, the thermal stability of the carbonates…
questions.why: Larger cations polarise the carbonate ion less, so it is harder to decompose.

questions.q: Concentrated H₂SO₄ is added to solid NaBr. Which is produced?
o: HBr and some Br₂ and SO₂
questions.why: Bromide is a strong enough reducing agent to reduce some of the sulfuric acid to SO₂.

questions.q: Silver nitrate gives a cream precipitate soluble in concentrated ammonia. Which halide?
questions.why: AgCl is white (dissolves in dilute NH₃), AgBr cream (concentrated), AgI yellow (insoluble).

questions.q: Why is N₂ unreactive?
o: Its triple bond is very strong
questions.why: N≡N has a high bond energy.

questions.q: Which pollutant forms when nitrogen and oxygen react in a hot engine?
questions.why: High temperatures let N₂ and O₂ combine to form nitrogen oxides.

questions.q: Structural isomers have the same…
questions.why: Same molecular formula, different structures.

questions.q: Why can but-2-ene show cis/trans (E/Z) isomerism?
o: There is restricted rotation about C=C with two different groups on each carbon
questions.why: Both conditions are needed for geometrical isomers.

questions.q: A chiral carbon has…
questions.why: It gives non-superimposable mirror images (optical isomers).

questions.q: Alkanes react with chlorine in UV light by…
questions.why: UV splits Cl₂ into radicals: initiation, propagation, termination.

questions.q: Ethene reacts with bromine by…
questions.why: The electron-rich C=C attacks the polarised Br₂.

questions.q: Which halogenoalkane hydrolyses fastest?
questions.why: The C–I bond is the weakest, so it breaks most easily.

questions.q: Heating a halogenoalkane with ethanolic KOH mainly gives…
questions.why: In ethanol, OH⁻ acts as a base and removes HX.

questions.q: Which alcohol is NOT oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI)?
questions.why: Tertiary alcohols have no H on the carbon bearing the OH.

questions.q: Distilling a primary alcohol with acidified dichromate as it forms gives…
questions.why: Distilling removes the aldehyde before it oxidises further; heating under reflux gives the acid.

questions.q: Which reagent distinguishes an aldehyde from a ketone?
questions.why: Aldehydes give a silver mirror; ketones don't. 2,4-DNPH reacts with both.

questions.q: NaBH₄ reduces a ketone to…
questions.why: Ketones are reduced to secondary alcohols.

questions.q: An alcohol and a carboxylic acid with a concentrated H₂SO₄ catalyst form…
questions.why: Esterification (a condensation reaction).

questions.q: Carboxylic acids react with sodium carbonate to give…
questions.why: They are acidic enough to release CO₂ from carbonates.

questions.q: A nitrile is hydrolysed by heating with dilute acid. It forms…
questions.why: R–C≡N + 2H₂O + H⁺ → RCOOH + NH₄⁺.

questions.q: Reacting a halogenoalkane with KCN in ethanol…
o: lengthens the carbon chain by one
questions.why: CN⁻ substitutes for the halogen, adding a carbon.

questions.q: What is the repeat unit of poly(propene)?
questions.why: Opening propene's C=C gives –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–.

questions.q: Why are poly(alkenes) hard to dispose of?
questions.why: Strong, non-polar C–C and C–H bonds; burning them can release toxic gases.

questions.q: To go from ethanol to ethanoic acid, use…
questions.why: Full oxidation of a primary alcohol under reflux.

questions.q: A broad IR absorption at 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ with a peak near 1700 cm⁻¹ suggests…
questions.why: Broad O–H (acid) plus C=O.

questions.q: In a mass spectrum, the M⁺ peak gives the…
questions.why: The molecular ion peak is at the Mr (the M+1 peak hints at the carbon count).

questions.q: A reaction is feasible when ΔG is…
questions.why: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS ≤ 0 for a feasible reaction.

questions.q: Lattice energy becomes more exothermic when ions are…
questions.why: Smaller, more highly charged ions attract more strongly.

questions.q: Which change has a positive entropy change?
o: A solid dissolving to make aqueous ions
questions.why: Particles become more disordered (more ways to arrange energy).

questions.q: Cu²⁺/Cu E° = +0.34 V and Zn²⁺/Zn E° = −0.76 V. What is the cell e.m.f.?
questions.why: E°cell = E°(positive) − E°(negative) = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V.

questions.q: How much charge passes when 0.20 A flows for 965 s? (F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹)
o: Both: 193 C, which is 0.0020 mol of electrons
questions.why: Q = It = 193 C; 193 ÷ 96 500 = 0.0020 mol of electrons.

questions.q: What is the pH of 0.010 mol dm⁻³ HCl?
A buffer resists pH change because…
o: it contains a weak acid and its conjugate base that remove added H⁺ or OH⁻
questions.why: Large reservoirs of HA and A⁻ absorb small additions.

questions.q: Ka for a weak acid is 1.0 × 10⁻⁵. What is its pKa?
questions.why: pKa = −log Ka = 5.

questions.q: Doubling [A] quadruples the rate. The order with respect to A is…
questions.why: rate ∝ [A]ⁿ and 2ⁿ = 4, so n = 2.

questions.q: The half-life of a first-order reaction…
questions.why: First-order half-lives are independent of concentration.

questions.q: Down Group 2, the solubility of the sulfates…
questions.why: Hydration enthalpy falls faster than lattice energy as the cation gets bigger.

questions.q: Why are transition metal compounds often coloured?
o: d-orbitals split in a ligand field and electrons absorb visible light moving between them
questions.why: The light not absorbed gives the complementary colour.

questions.q: What is the coordination number of [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺?
questions.why: Six water ligands form dative bonds to Cu²⁺.

questions.q: Which is a bidentate ligand?
questions.why: en forms two dative bonds through its two nitrogen atoms.

topics.name: Introduction to A Level organic chemistry

questions.q: Benzene's bond lengths are all equal because…
o: its π electrons are delocalised over the ring
questions.why: Delocalisation gives six identical C–C bonds between single and double.

questions.q: Benzene reacts with bromine in the presence of FeBr₃ by…
questions.why: Substitution keeps the stable delocalised ring.

questions.q: What is the electrophile in the nitration of benzene?
questions.why: Concentrated HNO₃ and H₂SO₄ form the nitronium ion NO₂⁺.

questions.q: Why is chlorobenzene much less reactive to nucleophiles than chloroalkanes?
o: The C–Cl bond is strengthened by overlap with the ring's π system
questions.why: Partial double-bond character makes the C–Cl bond harder to break.

questions.q: Phenol reacts with bromine water to give…
questions.why: The OH group activates the ring, so substitution happens readily without a catalyst.

questions.q: Which is the strongest acid?
questions.why: Order: ethanoic acid > phenol > water > ethanol.

questions.q: Acyl chlorides react with water to give…
questions.why: Vigorous hydrolysis with steamy HCl fumes.

questions.q: Why is phenylamine a weaker base than ethylamine?
o: The lone pair on N is delocalised into the ring, so it's less available
questions.why: Delocalisation reduces the lone pair's ability to accept a proton.

questions.q: Amino acids exist in solution near neutral pH as…
questions.why: The –COOH loses H⁺ and the –NH₂ gains it.

questions.q: A polyester is formed from…
o: a diol and a dicarboxylic acid
questions.why: Ester links form, eliminating water each time (condensation polymerisation).

questions.q: Which reagent converts a carboxylic acid to an acyl chloride?
questions.why: SOCl₂ (or PCl₅) replaces OH with Cl.

questions.q: In proton NMR, a peak split into a triplet has how many H on adjacent carbons?
questions.why: The n + 1 rule: n = 2 gives a triplet.

questions.q: Why is D₂O added in proton NMR?
o: To identify O–H and N–H protons, whose peaks disappear
questions.why: Deuterium exchanges with labile protons, removing their peaks.
